payload.title: [auth-core-5] findUserBySubject loads and linearly scans ALL User rows on every auth request
payload.description:
AUDIT FINDING auth-core-5 (low/dos, confidence=medium, verify-votes +2/-0)

FILE: apps/server/src/auth/identity-routes.ts
LINES: 2051-2059

WHAT: findUserBySubject calls store.listObjects(SYSTEM_TENANT, userObject.type) (L2057) to fetch EVERY User object into memory, then .find() scans for the matching subject/email. This runs on every email login, signup, forgot-password, and every apple/google/oidc/saml verify (e.g. L642, L788, L953, L1190, L1339, L1455, L1672). For email signup/login it is the first DB op and is unthrottled (see auth-core-1). With a large user table this is O(N) memory+CPU per unauthenticated request and a straightforward amplification/DoS vector; findPrimaryTenantForUser similarly lists all TenantMembership rows (L2068).

IMPACT: Auth endpoints degrade linearly with user count and can be driven to high CPU/memory by unauthenticated request floods; combined with the missing email-login throttle this is an inexpensive resource-exhaustion lever.

SUGGESTED FIX: Index the subject/email lookup in the store (indexed query by field value) instead of listObjects + in-memory find, and gate the unauthenticated paths behind the throttle.
